minor.issue: source_id filter is a no-op when the passed id has no root in the hierarchy index. index.root_for(source_id) returns None -> filter_root=None -> no filtering. The endpoint's own emitted source_ids (e.g. 'email:admin@bankezee.com') fall into this bucket, and any real user id whose canonical root is itself but is not in the hierarchy index is also affected. Suggested fix: `filter_root = index.root_for(source_id) or (source_id if source_id else None)` in _commission_report_data (files_crm.py:1782).

All 27 groups have source_name='Unassigned' because index.display_name(root) returns None for canonical roots keyed as 'email:...'. UI Commission panel therefore shows every GP group header as 'Unassigned' - major visible defect in the UI. Fix: fall back to lookup users collection by canonical id / email alias when display_name is empty.

ui_bugs.issue: Every GP-group card renders the group header/name as 'Unassigned' because backend source_name is 'Unassigned' for all 27 groups (see backend minor #2). Bank-details line under each GP also reads 'Not provided' for every field.

integration_issues.issue: Dropdown options carry the real users.id ObjectId but many GPs (e.g. asma.sultana0r@gmail.com id 6a5866a969071f897aef93a1) have 0 file disbursals AND their lead docs' source_id is not resolved to the same canonical id (leads reference by email:...). Selecting them returns 0 groups. Selecting Anusha does work (returns 1 group). Effectively the GP filter only works for GPs whose users.id is present in the hierarchy index root_for chain.

critical_code_review_comments: files_crm.py _commission_report_data lines 1782-1795: root_for(source_id) is the ONLY filter path; when it returns None the filter silently becomes a no-op. Fail-open on filters is dangerous - the report would return everyone even if a GP filter is set.

files_crm.py lines 1834-1835: source_id emitted uses `root` which for orphan GPs becomes 'email:xxx'. display_name(root) then can't find them. The GP CANONICAL id used to emit and the id used to look up bank_details/name must be consistent (either both users.id ObjectId or both 'email:...' with a matching resolver).
EarningsCard.js: no ESC/backdrop handler on modal is fine (modal has bg-black/50 onClick backdrop close). Code is clean.

FilesDashboard.js commission-bank-filter options derive from commissionData rows, so a bank that had ZERO matching rows in the currently filtered view disappears from the dropdown - a user-facing quirk if they had first filtered by bank and no rows came back. Non-blocking.

rca of the issue: Backend `_commission_report_data` uses `index.root_for(source_id)` to compute the canonical filter root AND to bucket every lead into a group. If the canonical root falls back to a synthetic key like 'email:foo@bar.com' (because the user doc/alias graph doesn't map that id to a real users.id), (a) `filter_root` becomes None -> filter is silently dropped, and (b) `display_name(root)` and `db.users.find_one({'id': {'$in': aliases}})` both return empty because no users.id equals 'email:foo@bar.com'. Result: correct SUMS (money is computed straight from stored eligibility.commission_amount) but 'Unassigned' display and a non-functional GP filter. Fix in files_crm.py: (1) `filter_root = index.root_for(source_id) or source_id` and match either root or source_id when filtering; (2) resolve display name & bank_details by trying users.find by email/aliases when the canonical root is an email:… key.
